_comment: Paths are on the Data volume. '~' is the scanned user's home. '*' matches one path segment and may be a glob like '*.photoslibrary'. Later rules win over earlier ones on the same folder. Safety: system, app-data, user-data, rebuilds, safe.

rules.info: Parts of macOS that live on the writable Data volume rather than the sealed system volume.
Assets macOS downloads on demand: Siri and dictation models, voices, fonts, Apple Intelligence models, and staged software updates.
Apps installed for all users.
Xcode.
Another user's home folder.
Files shared between all users of this Mac.
Your home folder.
A folder in your home. System Settings counts visible home folders as Documents.
A hidden folder in your home. System Settings counts hidden folders as System Data, which is a common reason System Data looks large.
Your Library folder: app settings, caches and data. Most of it counts as System Data.
Apps installed only for you.
Your Music folder.
Apple TV app downloads.
A Photos library.
Your Trash. Its space comes back only when you empty it.
iCloud Drive files kept on this Mac.
Messages history and attachments. Turning on Messages in iCloud lets macOS offload old attachments.
Mail's local copies of your mailboxes and attachments.
Xcode and simulator data: build products, device support files, simulators.
Command Line Tools, simulator runtimes and other developer files installed for all users.
GarageBand sound library.
Logic Pro sound library.
Apple Loops for GarageBand and Logic.
Settings, support files and plug-ins installed for all users.
System-wide caches. Safe to clear; rebuilt as needed.
Shared Adobe components used by Creative Cloud apps. Removed by Adobe's uninstallers.
OpenCore Legacy Patcher files. Only useful on unsupported Intel Macs.
Apple's Command Line Tools (compilers, git). Needed by Homebrew.
Unix system folders: variable data, temporary files, logs.
System databases.
Unified log storage. Erasing it removes all diagnostic log history.
Format strings the unified log needs to show messages.
Per-user temporary and cache folders managed by macOS.
The sleep image (a copy of memory written when the Mac hibernates).
Memory image written for hibernation. macOS manages its size.
Homebrew: installed packages (Cellar), shared files and its own git checkout.
Installed Homebrew packages. 'brew cleanup' removes old versions.
Software installed outside Homebrew on Apple Silicon (or Homebrew on Intel).
File system event log used by Spotlight, Time Machine and backup tools.
Spotlight index for the Data volume.
Saved versions of documents (File > Revert To).
App caches. Apps rebuild them, with slower first launches.
Downloaded Homebrew bottles. 'brew cleanup' removes them.
Browsers downloaded by Playwright.
App logs and crash reports.
App data. Each folder belongs to an app; deleting it resets or breaks that app.
An app's data folder. System Settings counts third-party app data under Applications.
Data of an Apple app or service.
Google Drive for desktop: its cache and database.
Google Drive's local copies of files you opened or pinned.
Copies Google Drive kept when an upload was cancelled. Check the files are in Drive, then remove.
Chrome profiles: history, extensions, site data and caches.
Claude desktop app data.
The Linux VM image Claude uses for Cowork on this Mac. Rebuilt if removed, but needed while Cowork runs.
Working folders from earlier Claude agent sessions.
Iris app data.
Iris cache.
Dropbox data, including a self-updating copy of Dropbox.app.
Zoom data, including downloaded updates.
Sandboxed apps' private folders.
A sandboxed app's private data. System Settings counts third-party app data under Applications.
Private data of an Apple app or service.
Messages share sheet data. Mostly attachment copies.
Safari data: caches, website data, reading list.
Messages app container.
Apple Maps tiles and location data cache.
Photos and video analysis results (faces, scenes).
Data shared between an app and its extensions.
Data shared between a third-party app and its extensions. Counted under Applications.
Data shared between Apple apps and services.
Data shared between Apple apps and services.
WhatsApp message history and media.
OrbStack Docker and Linux VM data.
Photos that Messages saved for Shared with You. Turn off Messages > Settings > Shared with You > Photos to stop it.
Spotlight's index of app content (mail, messages, notes).
On-device activity history Siri and suggestions learn from.
Private data of system background services.
Thunderbird mail profiles.
pnpm's shared package store. 'pnpm store prune' removes unused packages.
Xcode build products. Safe to clear; rebuilt on next build.
Debug symbols copied from each iPhone you connected. Recreated when you connect again.
App archives you built for distribution. Needed to symbolicate old crash reports.
iOS simulator devices and caches.
Simulator caches. Safe to clear.
Caches of command-line tools.
npm's download cache.
Android emulator images and settings.
Claude Code settings, history and plugins.
Codex CLI settings and history.
Docker CLI settings.
Rust toolchain packages.
VS Code extensions.
Apple Books downloads.
Downloaded podcast episodes.
Backups of iPhones and iPads made on this Mac.
